newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain's Telefonica to be fully privatised Feb 18.
newsitem.headline: Spain's Telefonica to be fully privatised Feb 18.

text.p: Spanish telecommunication's group Telefonica de Espana will be fully privatised on February 18, industry sources said on Thursday.
The sources said the communication company will issue the prospectus of the sale on January 17, while the retail tranche will be put on sale from January 20.
The state is offering 20.9 percent through its holding company SEPPa and another 0.11 percent through its main holding company.
On January 3, the national stock market commission CNMV said Spain had presented a share offer for 21.01 percent of the telecoms operator.
The offer will be divided into domestic and international tranches with the domestic tranche split between institutional and retail buyers.
On January 17, the prospectus will give details about the final number of shares on sale, the exact amount of the different tranches, and the Green Shoe.
Retail investors will get a four percent discount off the market reference price of the shares.
They will also receive one free share for every 20 in a "loyalty bonus" if they hold their investment from February 18, 1997 to February 19, 1998.
The special tranche for employees and pensioners of Telefonica and its majority-owned subsidiary may carry added incentives.
Global coordinators for the sale are: Argentaria, Banco Bilbao de Viscaya, La Caixa and Morgan Stanley.
Domestic directors for the institutional tranche are Argentaria, BBV, La Caixa, Banco Central Hispano-BCH and Banco Santander with Caja de Madrid in addition for the retail tranche.
The Banco Exterior de Espana-BEX will be named as the agent bank managing the offer.
